P0011.title: Intake Camshaft Timing Over-Advanced (Bank 1)
P0011.plain: The engine's valve timing is further ahead than the computer asked for. Low or dirty oil is often behind it.
P0011.tellMechanic: I have a P0011. Can you check the oil level and the cam timing solenoid first?

P0016.title: Crankshaft/Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 1 Sensor A)
P0016.plain: The crankshaft and camshaft aren't lined up the way the computer expects. That can mean the timing chain or belt has stretched or slipped.
causes: Stretched timing chain or slipped belt
Bad cam or crank position sensor
P0016.tellMechanic: I have a P0016 cam/crank correlation code. Can you check the timing chain and the VVT solenoid?

P0101.title: Mass Air Flow (MAF) Sensor Range/Performance
P0101.plain: The sensor that measures air coming into the engine is giving readings that don't make sense. The engine may run rough or hesitate.
causes: Air leak between the sensor and the engine
P0101.tellMechanic: I have a P0101. Can you clean or test the MAF sensor and check for intake leaks?

P0113.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P0113.plain: The sensor that reads incoming air temperature is sending a signal that's too high, usually because it's unplugged or its wiring is damaged.
P0113.tellMechanic: I have a P0113. Can you check the intake air temp sensor and its connector?

P0117.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P0117.plain: The engine temperature sensor is reporting an impossibly hot reading, usually from a wiring short or a bad sensor. Your temperature gauge and cooling fan may act oddly.
P0117.tellMechanic: I have a P0117. Can you test the coolant temperature sensor and its wiring?

P0118.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P0118.plain: The engine temperature sensor is reporting an impossibly cold reading, usually because it's unplugged or failed. Your temperature gauge and cooling fan may act oddly.
P0118.tellMechanic: I have a P0118. Can you test the coolant temperature sensor and its connector?

P0128.title: Coolant Thermostat (Coolant Temperature Below Regulating Temperature)
P0128.plain: Your engine is taking too long to warm up. Usually the thermostat is stuck open.
P0128.tellMechanic: I have a P0128. Can you check the thermostat and the coolant temp sensor?

P0133.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Slow Response (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P0133.plain: The oxygen sensor before the catalytic converter is reacting slowly, which can hurt fuel economy. It's often just an old sensor.
causes: Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor
P0133.tellMechanic: I have a P0133. Can you check for exhaust leaks before replacing the upstream O2 sensor?

P0135.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P0135.plain: The built-in heater in the oxygen sensor before the catalytic converter isn't working, so the sensor takes longer to start reading.
causes: Failed heater inside the oxygen sensor
Blown fuse for the sensor heater
P0135.tellMechanic: I have a P0135. Can you check the O2 heater fuse before replacing the sensor?

P0141.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P0141.plain: The built-in heater in the oxygen sensor after the catalytic converter isn't working.
causes: Failed heater inside the oxygen sensor
Blown fuse for the sensor heater
P0141.tellMechanic: I have a P0141. Can you check the O2 heater fuse and wiring for the downstream sensor?

P0171.title: System Too Lean (Bank 1)
P0171.plain: The engine is getting too much air or not enough fuel. A vacuum leak is the most common reason.
causes: Vacuum leak from a cracked hose
Weak fuel pump or clogged fuel filter
P0171.tellMechanic: I have a P0171 lean code. Can you smoke-test for vacuum leaks and check the MAF sensor?

P0172.title: System Too Rich (Bank 1)
P0172.plain: The engine is getting too much fuel for the amount of air. You might smell fuel or notice worse gas mileage.
P0172.tellMechanic: I have a P0172 rich code. Can you check the MAF sensor and fuel pressure?

P0174.title: System Too Lean (Bank 2)
P0174.plain: One side of the engine is getting too much air or not enough fuel. A vacuum leak is the most common reason.
causes: Vacuum leak from a cracked hose
Weak fuel pump or clogged fuel filter
P0174.tellMechanic: I have a P0174 lean code. Can you smoke-test for vacuum leaks and check the MAF sensor?

P0175.title: System Too Rich (Bank 2)
P0175.plain: One side of the engine is getting too much fuel for the amount of air. You might smell fuel or notice worse gas mileage.
P0175.tellMechanic: I have a P0175 rich code. Can you check the MAF sensor and fuel pressure?

P0217.title: Engine Overtemperature Condition
P0217.plain: Your engine has been overheating. Stop driving as soon as it's safe, because heat can warp or crack engine parts.
P0217.tellMechanic: I have a P0217 overheat code. Can you pressure-test the cooling system and check the fan?

P0300.title: Random/Multiple Cylinder Misfire Detected
P0300.plain: The engine is misfiring, meaning cylinders aren't firing properly. You may feel shaking or hesitation, and unburned fuel can damage the catalytic converter.
causes: Failing ignition coils or plug wires
P0300.tellMechanic: I have a P0300 random misfire. Can you check the plugs, coils, and look for vacuum leaks?

P0301.title: Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected
P0301.plain: Cylinder 1 isn't firing properly. You may feel shaking or hesitation, and unburned fuel can damage the catalytic converter.
causes: Failing ignition coil or plug wire
P0301.tellMechanic: I have a P0301. Can you swap the cylinder 1 coil with another cylinder to see if the misfire follows it?

P0302.title: Cylinder 2 Misfire Detected
P0302.plain: Cylinder 2 isn't firing properly. You may feel shaking or hesitation, and unburned fuel can damage the catalytic converter.
causes: Failing ignition coil or plug wire
P0302.tellMechanic: I have a P0302. Can you swap the cylinder 2 coil with another cylinder to see if the misfire follows it?

P0303.title: Cylinder 3 Misfire Detected
P0303.plain: Cylinder 3 isn't firing properly. You may feel shaking or hesitation, and unburned fuel can damage the catalytic converter.
causes: Failing ignition coil or plug wire
P0303.tellMechanic: I have a P0303. Can you swap the cylinder 3 coil with another cylinder to see if the misfire follows it?

P0304.title: Cylinder 4 Misfire Detected
P0304.plain: Cylinder 4 isn't firing properly. You may feel shaking or hesitation, and unburned fuel can damage the catalytic converter.
causes: Failing ignition coil or plug wire
P0304.tellMechanic: I have a P0304. Can you swap the cylinder 4 coil with another cylinder to see if the misfire follows it?

P0305.title: Cylinder 5 Misfire Detected
P0305.plain: Cylinder 5 isn't firing properly. You may feel shaking or hesitation, and unburned fuel can damage the catalytic converter.
causes: Failing ignition coil or plug wire
P0305.tellMechanic: I have a P0305. Can you swap the cylinder 5 coil with another cylinder to see if the misfire follows it?

P0306.title: Cylinder 6 Misfire Detected
P0306.plain: Cylinder 6 isn't firing properly. You may feel shaking or hesitation, and unburned fuel can damage the catalytic converter.
causes: Failing ignition coil or plug wire
P0306.tellMechanic: I have a P0306. Can you swap the cylinder 6 coil with another cylinder to see if the misfire follows it?

P0325.title: Knock Sensor 1 Circuit (Bank 1)
P0325.plain: The sensor that listens for engine knock isn't sending a good signal. The computer may play it safe and cut some power.
P0325.tellMechanic: I have a P0325. Can you check the knock sensor wiring before replacing the sensor?

P0335.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor A Circuit
P0335.plain: The computer lost the signal that tells it where the crankshaft is. The engine may stall or refuse to start.
causes: Damaged tone ring on the crankshaft
P0335.tellMechanic: I have a P0335. Can you check the crank sensor signal and its wiring?

P0340.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit (Bank 1)
P0340.plain: The computer isn't getting a good signal from the camshaft sensor. The car may be hard to start or run poorly.
P0340.tellMechanic: I have a P0340. Can you check the cam sensor and its wiring, and confirm the timing is right?

P0401.title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation (EGR) Flow Insufficient
P0401.plain: The system that sends a little exhaust back into the engine to lower emissions isn't flowing enough. You might hear pinging when accelerating.
P0401.tellMechanic: I have a P0401. Can you check the EGR passages for carbon buildup before replacing the valve?

P0411.title: Secondary Air Injection System Incorrect Flow
P0411.plain: The pump that blows fresh air into the exhaust at cold start isn't moving enough air. It only affects emissions for the first minute or so.
P0411.tellMechanic: I have a P0411. Can you check the air pump fuse and relay, and the check valve?

P0420.title: Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
P0420.plain: Your catalytic converter isn't cleaning the exhaust as well as it should.
P0420.tellMechanic: I have a P0420. Can you check the O2 sensors and look for exhaust leaks before replacing the converter?

P0430.title: Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
P0430.plain: The catalytic converter on one side of the engine isn't cleaning the exhaust as well as it should.
P0430.tellMechanic: I have a P0430. Can you check the O2 sensors and look for exhaust leaks before replacing the converter?

P0440.title: Evaporative Emission System Malfunction
P0440.plain: The system that traps gas fumes from your fuel tank found a problem. It doesn't affect how the car drives.
P0440.tellMechanic: I have a P0440. Can you smoke-test the EVAP system?

P0442.title: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Small Leak)
P0442.plain: The system that traps gas fumes has a small leak. Often it's just a gas cap that isn't sealing.
P0442.tellMechanic: I have a P0442. I've checked the gas cap. Can you smoke-test the EVAP system?

P0446.title: Evaporative Emission System Vent Control Circuit
P0446.plain: The valve that lets the fuel vapor system breathe isn't working right. It doesn't affect how the car drives.
causes: Damaged wiring to the vent valve
P0446.tellMechanic: I have a P0446. Can you check the EVAP vent valve and its wiring?

P0455.title: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Large Leak)
P0455.plain: The system that traps gas fumes has a big leak. Check that the gas cap is on and clicked tight first.
P0455.tellMechanic: I have a P0455. The gas cap is tight. Can you smoke-test the EVAP system?

P0456.title: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Very Small Leak)
P0456.plain: The system that traps gas fumes has a tiny leak. A gas cap with a worn seal is a common cause.
causes: Small crack in a vapor hose
P0456.tellMechanic: I have a P0456. Can you smoke-test the EVAP system for a small leak?

P0457.title: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Fuel Cap Loose/Off)
P0457.plain: Your gas cap is loose or missing. Tighten it until it clicks, and the light should go off after some driving.
P0457.tellMechanic: I have a P0457. I've tightened the gas cap. Could the cap seal be bad?

P0500.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor A
P0500.plain: The computer isn't getting a speed signal. Your speedometer may stop working, and an automatic transmission may shift oddly.
P0500.tellMechanic: I have a P0500. Can you check the speed sensor and its wiring?

P0505.title: Idle Air Control System
P0505.plain: The engine can't hold a steady idle. It may idle too high, too low, or stall at stops.
P0505.tellMechanic: I have a P0505. Can you clean the throttle body and check the idle air control valve?

P0524.title: Engine Oil Pressure Too Low
P0524.plain: Your engine oil pressure is too low. Stop driving as soon as it's safe and check the oil level, because low oil pressure can ruin an engine fast.
P0524.tellMechanic: I have a P0524. Can you check the actual oil pressure with a gauge?

P0562.title: System Voltage Low
P0562.plain: The car's electrical system voltage is too low. The battery or alternator may be on its way out.
P0562.tellMechanic: I have a P0562. Can you test the battery and the alternator output?

P0606.title: Control Module Processor Fault
P0606.plain: The engine computer found a problem with itself. Sometimes a software update fixes it; sometimes the computer needs replacing.
causes: Poor power or ground to the computer
P0606.tellMechanic: I have a P0606. Can you check the computer's power and grounds, and whether there's a software update?

P0700.title: Transmission Control System Malfunction
P0700.plain: The transmission computer found a problem and saved its own code. A transmission scan will show the details.
causes: A fault stored in the transmission computer
P0700.tellMechanic: I have a P0700. Can you read the transmission computer's codes?
